solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Illness mostly found in horses spreads

indicators.note: mostly means most but not all of the word, so its final letter is dropped
something found in another thing sits inside it, so one piece goes within the other

explanation.surface: A vet notes that a sickness is turning up among the horses and spreading.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spreads' reads as a verb about the illness; it is the plural noun for things put on bread.
explanation.definitionFit: Marmalades are citrus preserves that people spread on toast, so they are spreads in the food sense.

clue.text: Type of post Irishman Brian unwrapped then erected

indicators.note: unwrapping strips off the outer covering, so the first and last letters of the name go
in a down entry, putting something upright means it reads from the bottom upwards

blocks.note: Liam is a common Irish first name

explanation.surface: An Irishman named Brian unwraps a parcel and stands it up, puzzling over its postage.
explanation.walkthrough: LIAM plus RIA gives LIAMRIA, which read upwards in the down light becomes the answer. 'Irishman Brian' looks like one man; it is two separate pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Airmail is mail sent by aircraft, one class or kind of postal service.

clue.text: Small child's pronounced strength

indicators.note: pronounced means spoken out, so the word is wanted by its sound rather than its spelling

blocks.note: a mite is a small child; the 's is just 'is'

explanation.surface: A tiny child's strength is said to be remarkable.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Small child's' reads as possessive; it is 'small child is', joining wordplay to definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Might is power or force, a direct synonym for strength.

clue.text: Coffee line adopted by railway recently

indicators.note: a thing adopted by another is taken in by it, so it goes inside

blocks.note: a latte is a milky coffee
RY is the standard abbreviation for railway
L is the abbreviation for line

explanation.surface: A railway has lately started serving coffee to the queue of passengers.
explanation.walkthrough: The line letter goes inside the railway abbreviation, not inside the coffee.
explanation.definitionFit: Latterly is an adverb meaning in the recent past, matching recently in sense and part of speech.

clue.text: Fellow and park officer after beginning to track animal keep in touch

indicators.note: the beginning of a word is its opening letter, so only that one is kept
after places one part behind the run of parts before it in the answer

blocks.note: a don is a fellow of a university college
a park ranger looks after a park

explanation.surface: A fellow and a park ranger go off to track an animal, promising to stay in contact.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue names the park officer first, but 'after' sends that piece to the very end of the phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: Don't be a stranger is a friendly parting phrase urging someone to stay in contact, the same plea as keep in touch.

clue.text: Not married, appearing to be discerning

indicators.note: not marks that the following abbreviation is removed from the word

blocks.note: M is the abbreviation for married
seeming means appearing, as in seeming to be

explanation.surface: A single person seems to be choosy about partners.
explanation.walkthrough: SEEMING loses its M to leave the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Seeing can mean perceptive or understanding, as in a seeing eye, so it fits discerning.

clue.text: Found singer in audition

indicators.note: an audition is a hearing, so the word is taken by how it sounds

blocks.note: a bass is a low male singer

explanation.surface: A talent scout discovers a singer while hearing hopefuls try out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Found' looks like the past tense of find; here it is the verb to found, establish.
explanation.definitionFit: To base something is to found or ground it on something, as in a story based on fact.

clue.text: Learner taken in by deceptive person in attempts to win games

indicators.note: taken in by means received inside, so one piece sits within the other
in places the combined piece inside the next word

blocks.note: bids are attempts to win, as at an auction
L is the learner plate abbreviation

explanation.surface: A novice is fooled by a cheat while trying to win some games.
explanation.walkthrough: The learner's letter is inserted just after the first letter of the deceiver, and that whole piece then splits the attempts after their second letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Billiards is a cue sport; the plural noun names the game, matching games as a class.

clue.text: Mixed slammer with wine

indicators.note: with sets the second part alongside the first, one after the other

blocks.note: stir is slang for prison, as is slammer

explanation.surface: A cocktail of jail time and drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mixed' looks like an anagram signal; it is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: To stir something is to mix it with a spoon, so stirred is a past-tense synonym of mixed.

clue.text: Show off dress twirling round

indicators.note: twirling round turns the word to face the other way, so it reads backwards

explanation.surface: Someone shows off a new frock by spinning around in it.
explanation.definitionFit: To brag is to boast, which is to show off verbally.

clue.text: Crumpled old tenner secures one cut of meat

indicators.note: something crumpled is crushed out of shape, so the letters are jumbled
to secure is to hold fast inside, so the jumble wraps around the next piece

blocks.note: I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A creased old ten-pound note is used to buy a single piece of meat.
explanation.walkthrough: A tenner is a British ten-pound note. The Roman numeral for one lands near the end of the jumbled letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Tenderloin is the tender muscle along a loin, a particular butcher's cut.

clue.text: Guy consuming books for role

indicators.note: consuming means swallowing up, so one word takes the other inside it

blocks.note: NT is the New Testament, a set of books

explanation.surface: A man devours books in preparation for playing a part.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Books' in crosswords often means one of the two Testaments of the Bible.
explanation.definitionFit: A mantle is a responsibility or position passed on, as in taking up the mantle, which is a role.

clue.text: Detective shot following arrest to overturn organised crime

indicators.note: overturning flips the word over, so it reads backwards
following places one part behind another in the answer

blocks.note: a shot is an attempt, a try

explanation.surface: A detective takes a shot at overturning a gangland conviction.
explanation.walkthrough: NAB read backwards gives BAN, which comes first, followed by DI and TRY.
explanation.definitionFit: Banditry is robbery by organised gangs of bandits, hence organised crime.

clue.text: Occupy gathering group with a craft collection

indicators.note: gathering means collecting in, so one word encloses the other
with adds the next piece alongside, at the end

blocks.note: to fill a space is to occupy it
a lot is a group or batch

explanation.surface: Protesters occupy a building, gathering a group to make things at a craft fair.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Craft' suggests handicrafts; here it means boats.
explanation.definitionFit: A flotilla is a small fleet of boats, and craft is a word for vessels.

clue.text: Taxes kept being changed — OMG, WTF?!

indicators.note: being changed means altered into another form, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: An outraged reaction to news that taxes keep being altered.
explanation.definitionFit: OMG and WTF are abbreviations typical of text messaging shorthand, so they are examples of that style.

clue.text: Sit on free pew away from outsiders

indicators.note: keeping away from the outsiders strips the outer letters and leaves the centre

explanation.surface: Someone takes a free seat on a church pew, away from the crowd.
explanation.definitionFit: To ride a horse or bike is to sit on it and be carried along.

clue.text: Crushed, Edward is forbidden from socialising

blocks.note: ground is crushed, as with coffee

explanation.surface: Poor Edward is crushed at being kept in by his parents.
explanation.definitionFit: A grounded child is punished by being kept at home, not allowed out to see friends.

clue.text: Regularly picked Apple social media site as top

indicators.note: picking at regular intervals takes every other letter

blocks.note: X is the platform formerly called Twitter

explanation.surface: Apple and a social network both claim to be at the peak of the tech world.
explanation.definitionFit: The apex is the highest point or summit of something, synonymous with top.

clue.text: Irreverent teacher contracted again

indicators.note: contracted means shortened, so the last letter is cut

explanation.surface: A disrespectful teacher has been hired once more.
explanation.definitionFit: Profane describes language or acts that show disrespect for sacred things, so it means irreverent.

clue.text: Performing trio seem boring

indicators.note: performers act things out in a new arrangement, so the letters are reworked

explanation.surface: A critic finds a band of three dull on stage.
explanation.definitionFit: Tiresome means tedious and wearying, a close synonym of boring.

clue.text: This writer's beginning to refine aluminium ore

indicators.note: the beginning of a word is its first letter, which alone is kept

blocks.note: this writer is the setter, so what is the writer's is mine
Al is the chemical symbol for aluminium

explanation.surface: The setter claims to have begun refining aluminium from rock.
explanation.definitionFit: An ore is a naturally occurring mineral from which metal is extracted, so the two are close in sense.

clue.text: Trainees dance at the wings in musical show

indicators.note: the wings are the edges, so only the outermost letters are kept
in places the selected letters inside the following word

blocks.note: Cats is the Andrew Lloyd Webber musical
first and last letters of dance

explanation.surface: Novice performers dance in the wings during a musical.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wings' suggests the sides of a stage, fitting the scene, but here it means the edges of the word dance.
explanation.definitionFit: Cadets are young people training for the armed forces or police, so they are trainees.

clue.text: Land snake constricts tense bird

indicators.note: constricting means squeezing round something, as a constrictor does, so one word wraps the rest

blocks.note: a boa is a constricting snake
T is the grammatical abbreviation for tense

explanation.surface: A snake on land squeezes a nervous bird.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tense' looks like an adjective for the bird; it is an abbreviation. T and SWAN go inside BOA.
explanation.definitionFit: Botswana is a country in southern Africa, and land is a common word for a nation.

clue.text: Dire amateur gently boxes

indicators.note: a pair of words that boxes something encloses it, so the answer sits within them

blocks.note: the letters run across the join of the two words

explanation.surface: A hopeless novice spars softly in the ring.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Boxes' paints a boxing match; it means the two words enclose the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Dire can mean pressing or desperate, as in dire need, which is urgent.

clue.text: New information intercepted by soldiers

indicators.note: something intercepted is cut into midway, so the other piece breaks into it

explanation.surface: Fresh intelligence is seized by troops before it arrives.
explanation.definitionFit: Green describes someone inexperienced or newly started, as a green recruit is new to the job.

clue.text: Got trousers on the Parisian wearing just pants?

indicators.note: used as a verb, to trouser is to pocket, so one word takes the others inside

blocks.note: to bag is to get or seize

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether a man got his trousers on, or is he in just his underwear.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Trousers' looks like clothing in the picture; it is a verb meaning pockets. The question mark flags a playful definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone in only underpants has bare legs, which is what the adjective describes.

clue.text: Deserve attention with first from Newcastle

indicators.note: first from takes only the opening letter of the place

blocks.note: to have someone's ear is to have their attention

explanation.surface: A football club wants its fair share of notice.
explanation.definitionFit: To earn something is to deserve it through effort, as in earn respect.

clue.text: Adorn part of skateboard

blocks.note: second meaning: the flat board a skater stands on

explanation.surface: A skater decorates the board.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is both a verb for decorating and the noun for the standing surface of a skateboard.

clue.text: Shrewd holding spear in domineering manner

indicators.note: holding means keeping something within, so one word goes inside the other

blocks.note: a trident is a three-pronged spear

explanation.surface: A crafty warrior grips a spear and lords it over others.
explanation.walkthrough: A trident is the three-pronged spear carried by Neptune.
explanation.definitionFit: Stridently means in a loud, harsh and forceful way, the overbearing tone of someone who dominates.
